points.text: Variance of first-order EAP-IG circuits is expected; main finding unsurprising.
Number of samples used for attribution scores not reported.
Only EAP-IG circuit discovery studied; other methods neglected, limiting breadth.
No dedicated limitations section.
Claim that circuits fail to transfer across settings not well supported.
Presentation fixes: undefined DNN, caption placement, Table/Figure reference.
Last two paragraphs on page 7 are repetitive.
Interpretability proxy metric description incomplete.
Intervention noise procedure insufficiently described.
Model used for Table 1 not specified.
Instruction-tuning finding should cite consistent prior literature.
Stability metrics uninformative without circuit identifiability; parallel pathways and self-repair.
Circuits under different ablation methods or data shifts may not be comparable.
Instability not shown to come from EAP scoring rather than discretization/Jaccard.
Circuit errors very high; EAP poorly calibrated; compare stability at fixed error.
Experimental setup details lacking.
Analysed circuits largely unfaithful; should use error threshold and compare sizes.
Comparing circuit error while ignoring circuit size is misleading.
Lack of attention to detail, e.g. repeated paragraph; suggests other errors.
Jaccard on variable-size circuits mostly measures size mismatch; need fixed-k analysis.
Table 1 averages over different cells across perturbation conditions.
Dataset size and replicate count unstated; bootstrap vs meta-dataset gap unexplained.
Path-existence stop rule yields non-functional high-error circuits; need fixed faithfulness.
Circuit-performance metric insensitive to circuit; M_C evaluation undefined.
No reference scale or null baseline for calling variance high.
Pairwise statistics and CV inappropriate variance estimates; multimodality untested.
Noise experiment thin; amplitude unscaled, fixed direction; recommendation overreaches.
Caption and cross-reference inconsistencies, CV wording, 'three architectures'.
Table 1 paragraph duplicated in Section 5.1.
Typos and undefined median construction.
Jaccard confounded by circuit size; no size-controlled comparison.
Variance conflated with non-identifiability; no cross-evaluation of circuits.
Faithful circuit defined by path existence despite high errors.
Claims about larger models, instruction tuning and broad applicability overreach narrow evidence.
Identical circuit error/KL across sizes suggests insensitive or undefined metric.
Table 1 cross-strategy averages cover different cells.
Repeated Table 1 paragraph and typo.
Figure caption, table reference and architecture wording inconsistencies.
Should use stability selection and per-edge inclusion frequencies instead of Jaccard tables.
Notion of true circuit left open; recommendations lack actionable guidance.
Small models, templated prompts, single method; scaling extrapolation unsupported.
Noise amplitude recommendation not portable across models.
Novelty claim under-argued; closest statistical and circuit-variation works not differentiated.
Statistical estimation framing not carried through: no estimand, intervals or tests.
Variance conflated with non-identifiability; need functional cross-evaluation.
Several cited works mischaracterized.
Missing references on stability selection and related circuit work.
No yardstick to judge whether Jaccard variance is high.
Dataset size, replicates and defaults not stated.
Duplicated results paragraph.
Wrong table cross-reference and contradictory Figure 4 caption.
Conclusions about larger models, instruction tuning, broad applicability exceed scope.
Statistical stability literature not covered in related work.
Codebase claimed public but no link given.
No limitations section.

P.summary: Main finding unsurprising given first-order approximation.
Experimental setup details (sample count, model, noise procedure) missing.
Only one circuit discovery method studied.
Circuit identifiability not addressed; multiple valid circuits.
Circuits across ablation methods/data shifts not comparable.
Instability source (scoring vs discretization) not separated.
High-error circuits; stability should be at fixed faithfulness.

Q.summary: Dataset size and replicate count unstated.
Path-existence rule yields non-functional circuits; need fixed faithfulness.
No reference scale or baseline for high variance.
Inappropriate variance statistics; use per-edge inclusion/stability selection.
Noise experiment thin and amplitude not portable.
Conclusions overgeneralize beyond small models and one method.
True circuit undefined; recommendations not actionable.
Novelty under-argued; related statistical work missing.
Estimation framing lacks estimand and intervals.
